description:
An envelope addressed to a `(to, handle)` queue. Queues are the substrate primitive: the same shape carries direct messages (`to == peer_did`, handle `inbox:default`), local captures (`to == self_did`, handle `inbox:triage` etc.), and multi-subscriber channel posts (`to == owner_did`, handle `channel:dommage-corporel:paris-cohort`). Routing rule is `to == self_did?`: matching means stay-on-disk; non-matching means deliver to the owner's relay (the owner-as-sequencer invariant). Stamps are allowed on any envelope regardless of recipient — including self-attestations of one's own captures. In MVP the cryptographic stamp covers only the body, not the envelope.

**v0.3 channel addressing.** `to` is the *queue owner's* DID (the principal whose relay sequences the queue). `handle` is the colon-pathed queue address on that owner's machine — see `tech.equanimi.secretariat.channelDef` for the full handle grammar. The pair `(to, handle)` is the canonical wire address for any queue; the composite URI form `<to>#<handle>` (e.g. `did:web:themia.pro#channel:dommage-corporel:paris-cohort`) is **display-only** and never appears on the wire. The two fields stay factored so that resolvers, indexers, and roster checks can dispatch on `to` without parsing.

**Rationale for additive shape (Slice 1.5).** Bilateral DMs are not a separate case — a DM is a channel-of-two whose queue owner is the recipient peer and whose handle is `inbox:default`. The substrate already factors `(owner, handle)` (mirrored in the Rust `Recipient { owner, handle }` aggregate); the v0.3 channel-addressing requirement is fully expressible without new fields. This update tightens the description to make the canonical URI grammar explicit, cross-references `channelDef.handle` for the handle alphabet, and clarifies back-compat semantics for legacy v0.2.x envelopes.

**Legacy back-compat.** Pre-v0.3 peer-letter envelopes were written without `to` and `handle` (they carried only `from` and an implicit single-inbox destination). Readers MUST tolerate envelopes that omit `handle`, synthesizing `inbox:default`. Envelopes that also omit `to` are addressed to the reader's own DID by transport context (the envelope arrived in *my* inbox) — readers synthesize `to = self_did`. New writers MUST emit both fields.

from.description: DID of the sender (the principal whose scribe composed this envelope).

to.description: DID of the queue *owner* — the principal whose relay sequences this queue (per the owner-as-sequencer invariant). For direct messages this is the recipient peer; for local captures this is the principal themselves; for org-owned multi-subscriber channels this is the org's DID (typically a `did:web` rooted on a domain the org controls). Together with `handle` forms the canonical wire address for the queue; the composite URI `<to>#<handle>` is display-only.

handle.description: Queue handle on the owner's machine, colon-pathed for tree nesting. Form: `<namespace>:<segment>[:<segment>...]` where `namespace` is `inbox` for local single-owner queues (`inbox:default`, `inbox:triage`), `area` for principal-organized buckets (`area:health`, `area:writing`), and `channel` for org-owned multi-subscriber queues (`channel:dommage-corporel:paris-cohort`). Tree depth = colon depth. See `tech.equanimi.secretariat.channelDef.handle` for the full grammar — channel queues advertised by an org MUST use a handle that appears in the org's `orgDoc.channels`. Direct messages conventionally use `inbox:default`. Legacy v0.2.x envelopes omit this field; readers synthesize `inbox:default` for back-compat. New writers (v0.3+) MUST emit it.

depth.description: Declared attentional depth. Gross = surface-level, can be acknowledged peripherally. Subtle = needs deeper engagement.

urgency.description: Declared urgency. Inflationary by nature; the receiver-published attentionEnvelope constrains what is accepted.

source.description: Free-form origin of the work (e.g. Claude session ID, manual, agent name). Useful for retrospective traceability.

cadenceHint.description: Optional advisory hint to the receiver about when to surface (e.g. `morning`, `weekly`).

replyTo.description: Optional `DocHash` of a prior envelope's body that this envelope is replying to (form `sha256:<hex>`). Threads are chains of `replyTo` links; the root envelope of a thread omits this field. Wire-level only — thread materialization (collapsing a chain into an adapter's conversation view, e.g. Crisp session, Intercom thread) is the adapter's concern. Causality is cryptographic: the referenced hash must match a body the receiver actually has (or can request) for the link to verify, but the substrate does not enforce reachability — orphan replies are valid envelopes whose parent may arrive later or never.
